items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1959-09-01
items.q: Sidney Desvien and Amos White are on the record.

ctx.x: He's a big fella? Not too big.
Amos White and Sidney Desvien on the record. What? Sidney Desvien and Amos White are on the record. That's bad.

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-04-04
items.q: Sidney Desveen. All them used to play out there.

ctx.x: What were the names of the bands?
Well, René, Beout De Petit, Chris Kelly, maybe Sam Morgan, Sidney Desveen. All them used to play out there.
All of them. And what were some of the places there?

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1959-09-25
items.q: This Desveen fellow too, he had a nice reading band.

ctx.x: But who had the straight bands, you know, straight reading bands other than.
Well Robichaud and Tuxedo did a lot of reading. But after that, them other fellows, they weren't doing much reading. This Desveen fellow too, he had a nice reading band.

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1957-multiple
items.q: The Dine, downtown there, Cindy Desvinge, the old tuxedo, all them bands used to be out on the street

ctx.x: Who did you meet in the street, some of the different bands?

Well, every Sunday you'd meet a bunch, but it'd be the same bunch like Rene, Buddy Petit, Sam Marock, Chris Kelly, and what's his name? The Dine, downtown there, Cindy Desvinge, the old tuxedo, all them bands used to be out on the street, you know, advertising dances on Sundays. Maybe one of them would be playing at a funeral or something, somebody would die, and they'd all get on that together.
Did you ever have any battles of music in the places like, say, the Bows Club or any of those?
